title: Human-induced environmental change
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:50Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The new point covers human change to air and water pollution, species loss, and degraded land, rivers and seas, while the closest bank point, Land degradation, covers only land decline (erosion, salinity, vegetation loss) and the other is about the general idea of interconnection.

draft.title: Human-induced environmental change
card: Human-induced environmental change is change to an environment that is caused by human activity, not by natural processes alone.
harmful substances added to air, water or soil. Examples are smoke from burning fuels and fertiliser or sewage washed into rivers.
a fall in the number of plant and animal species. It can happen when people clear the land where species live.
damage that lowers the quality of land, rivers or seas. Examples are eroded soil, salty land and rivers choked with sediment.
draft.remember: People can change environments by polluting them, losing species and degrading land, rivers and seas.

a.q: Farmers clear bushland for crops, and a local frog species loses its habitat and disappears from the area. Which type of change is this?
opts: Loss of plant and animal species
a.why: The frogs disappear because people cleared their habitat, so the change is a loss of species. Nothing harmful was added to the air or water, which is why it is not pollution.
a.clue: What happened to the living things in the area?

b.q: Fertiliser from a sugar cane farm in Queensland washes into a creek. The creek turns green and the fish die. What is the main type of change that began this?
opts: Natural change with no human cause
b.why: Fertiliser is a substance that people added to the water, so it is water pollution. The fish deaths are a result. They show how one change can lead to others, but the change that started it was the added fertiliser.
b.clue: Look at what people added to the creek.

a.best: Loss of plant and animal species
